title: Brought duplicate-code detection to Philips, and teams removed 18,688 lines
summary: I introduced an open-source duplicate-code detector to Philips and built the program around it, with guides, a hands-on workshop and a before-and-after report teams could run themselves. With a senior director as sponsor, I ran workshops across business units, and teams I worked with removed 18,688 lines of duplicate code.
what_would_have_happened: Duplicate code grew unnoticed, so every fix had to be made in several places.
the_call: Measure duplication with a free tool teams can run themselves, and pair every report with a hands-on session.
what_i_did: Introduced the tool, wrote the installation and usage guides, designed the workshop and the before-and-after reporting template, ran sessions from September 2019 and compiled the results for leadership.
what_changed: Developers across at least six business units ran the tool and reported back; a senior director asked for a mechanism to remove 23% of duplicate code; teams I influenced removed 18,688 duplicate lines.

quotes.text: Great Datta. It provides good insight. As next step we need to devise mechanism to remove and commit 23% of duplicate code.
